q: In a scientific perspective, static electricity occurs when there is an imbalance of charges between two ____.
e: In a scientific perspective, static electricity occurs when there is an imbalance of charges between two objects. Electrostatics is charge at rest. Like charges push apart.

q: Static electricity can build up as a result of collisions among the molecules in ____.
e: Static electricity can build up as a result of collisions among the molecules in clouds. Electrostatics is charge at rest. Like charges push apart involving result.

q: This can cause a huge spark to form between the ground and the ____.

e: This causes a lightning discharge, therefore, a flow of charge through the atmosphere. The physics in this sentence is built around atmosphere.

q: As aircraft fly through the air, they can become charged with static ____.
e: As aircraft fly through the air, they can become charged with static electricity. The physics in this sentence is built around electricity.

q: A build-up of static charge is a potential danger when refuelling aircraft or ____.
e: A build-up of static charge is a potential danger when refuelling aircraft or vehicles. The physics in this sentence is built around vehicles.

q: Fuel running through the pipes can provide the friction needed to create a static ____.
e: Fuel running through the pipes can provide the friction needed to create a static charge. Charge here means the electric property that makes objects attract or repel.

q: To prevent this, aircraft are earthed with a conductor during ____.
e: To prevent this, aircraft are earthed with a conductor during refuelling. A conductor has plenty of free electrons, so charge can move.

q: Fuel tankers (bowsers) that transport fuel on roads must be earthed before any fuel is transferred, to prevent sparks causing a fire or ____.
e: Fuel tankers (bowsers) that transport fuel on roads must be earthed before any fuel is transferred, to prevent sparks causing a fire or explosion. The physics in this sentence is built around explosion.
